text.p: Tight nearby backwardations and falling London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks helped to drive three months delivery aluminium higher by the close of business on Friday. Elsewhere, unable to absorb a further LME stocks rise copper drifted, while tin on short-covering against the backdrop of uptrending charts moved to settle above $5,600 a tonne.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index added 0.61 points to 243.36.

Traders said aluminium received a boost from further investment fund buying following a breach above expected resistance at $1,725. Last business was seen at $1,739, one dollar down on its 21-month high of but a gain of $38 from Thursday's LME kerb close.
A narrowing of nearby spreads and a further inventory increase knocked copper lower to $2,309.50, down from $2,311.
Tin correcting from a recent oversold condition moved higher on short-covering and trade covering. It was last at $5,640, up $95.

Nickel moved $55 higher to $7,485 on news that Falconbridge's 1,400 unionised workers at its Sudbury, Ontario operations are on strike after union and company negotiators failed to agree on a new contract.
Lead was quiet and settled at $639, versus $632.
Alloy was last quoted higher AT $1,540 against $1,515/25 following the rise in the primary market.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly higher Friday, as gold and silver continued to consolidate after seeing multi-year lows last month, while platinum group metals (PGMs) recovered further to set new contract highs. COMEX December gold ended up 30 cents at $328.90 an ounce, but not before slipping to its lows for the week early at $327.30 an ounce. COMEX gold saw its lightest volume day this week though at 31,000 lots. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $324.40/90, compared with the London Friday afternoon fix at $324.10 and the New York close Thursday at $324.30/80.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mixed with late hedge pressure partly offset by a turn higher in the corn pit which triggered short covering in wheat, traders said. Wheat closed 1/2 cent per bushel lower to 4-1/2 cents higher, with September down 1/2 at $3.61-1/2 per bushel.

IPE gas oil futures closed firmer on Friday, buoyed by refinery problems in northwest Europe and a reversal of losses on crude futures, traders said. August gas oil ended $2.25 a tonne firmer at $171.50, but brokers noted that volumes were thin. September Brent recovered from a low of $18.63 and at 1730 GMT was trading at $18.91 a barrel, three cents off Thursday's close.
